newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish credit growth too high for comfort - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Irish credit growth too high for comfort - analysts.

text.p: DUBLIN, Dec 5 (Reuter) Higher-than-expected private sector credit growth data for October is likely to cause a knee-jerk reaction in shorter dated government paper but unlikely to lead to an interest rate rise, economists said on Thursday.

"We were forecasting at the top end of expectations and they even shocked ourselves," Goodbody Stockbrokers economist Aisling Riley told Reuters. "They were much stronger than expected, including the mortgage lending growth."
The adjusted annual growth rate of Irish private-sector credit grew to 14.3 percent in October from 13.3 percent at end-September.
The annual rate of increase in residential mortgage lending by all credit institutions rose to 17.1 percent from 16.5 percent.
Economists forecasts had ranged from 13.2 to 14 percent for private sector credit growth while residential mortgage lending forecasts ranged from 16.5 to 16.7 percent.
"The number is certainly bond-unfriendly but reaction should mainly be contained to the short-end," one economist said. "I do not see the central bank panicking and raises rates on the back of them."
